Submission checklist

Before submitting, check scope, originality, all author approvals, anonymisation, ethical declarations, references, and permissions.

Manuscript submission opens after OJS activation.

General requirements

Manuscripts should contribute to integrative social sciences and connect the research question, conceptual framework, methods, and conclusions. General descriptions or compilations without analysis are insufficient.

  • Submit original work that is not under consideration elsewhere.
  • All authors must have read and approved the manuscript and meet authorship contributions.
  • Use clear, consistent academic Indonesian or English.
  • Disclose funding, competing interests, and relevant ethics approvals.

Format & length

Use Microsoft Word (.docx), A4 pages, 2.5 cm margins, Times New Roman 12 pt, 1.5 line spacing, and page numbers. Article length is 4,000–8,000 words excluding references and appendices.

Download the manuscript and separate title-page templates below. Remove guidance text and identifying information from the manuscript before double-anonymous review.

Title & abstract

  • Title: concise and specific, reflecting the question and contribution without unfamiliar abbreviations.
  • Author details: full names, affiliations, countries, and corresponding-author email on a separate title page. Include ORCID when available.
  • Abstract: 150–250 words in Indonesian and English, covering aims, methods or approach, findings or main argument, and contribution.
  • Keywords: 3–5 terms representing the main concepts and subject.

Article structure

  • Introduction: context, problem, literature gap, aims, and contribution.
  • Conceptual framework: theories and connections across perspectives.
  • Methods: design, context, data sources, selection of participants or materials, analysis, and ethics.
  • Findings and discussion: evidence or argument in relation to the literature, including limitations.
  • Conclusion: answer the aims and explain implications without introducing new findings.
  • Declarations: author contributions, funding, competing interests, data availability, and acknowledgements where relevant.
  • References: only works cited in the manuscript.

Conceptual papers may adapt the structure to their argument. Reviews should explain literature selection and synthesis.

Citations & references

Use APA 7th edition as the journal style. Use consistent author–date citations, for example Name (2024) or (Name, 2024). Include page locators for direct quotations as appropriate to the source.

Every citation must match a reference entry and vice versa. Include DOI links when available. Verify names, dates, titles, and publication details; reference software does not replace checking.

Tables, figures & data

  • Number tables and figures in order, provide titles, and refer to them in the text.
  • Use legible figures and editable tables; explain abbreviations and data sources.
  • Obtain permission for third-party materials when required.
  • Avoid unnecessary personal identifiers, particularly in interview extracts and appendices.
  • State where supporting data can be accessed or explain restrictions related to confidentiality or participant consent.

Submission files

The journal uses double-anonymous review. Submit author details on a separate title page and remove identifying information from the main manuscript, file properties, acknowledgements, and supplementary material intended for reviewers.

  • A title page with author details, affiliations, contact email, and declarations.
  • An anonymised main manuscript, including document properties.
  • Figures and supplementary files where needed, with sources and captions.
  • A short cover letter explaining scope fit and contribution.

This preview does not accept uploads. Submissions will use OJS after installation and the official opening of submissions.

Submission checklist

  • The focus and integrative contribution are clear.
  • The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere.
  • Author details, abstracts, keywords, tables, figures, and references are complete.
  • Sources, permissions, funding, and competing interests are disclosed.
  • All authors approve the submitted version.
  • The current guidelines and templates have been checked.

Editorial workflow

The journal follows the OJS editorial stages: submission and screening, double-anonymous review by two reviewers, revision, copyediting, production, and publication.

  • Submission: authors enter metadata and upload files once the service opens.
  • Screening: editors assess completeness, scope, and readiness for review.
  • Review: reviewers provide scholarly assessments; editors may request revisions or decline the paper.
  • Revision: authors submit changes with a structured response to comments.
  • Copyediting and production: language editing, layout, proof checking, and final approval.
  • Publication: completed articles are assigned to an issue by the editors.

Acceptance is based on editorial assessment, not payment. No guaranteed acceptance or decision time is offered. The online workflow becomes available after OJS activation.
